title: The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains
authors: Pelland JC, Remmert JF, Robinson ZP, Hinson SR, Zourdos MC.
claim: Direct versus indirect set accounting was compared in meta-regressions; half-credit indirect sets fit best.
limitations: Does not validate quarter credit or any exercise-specific coefficient.

title: Interpreting Signal Amplitudes in Surface Electromyography Studies in Sport and Rehabilitation Sciences
authors: Vigotsky AD, Halperin I, Lehman GJ, Trajano GS, Vieira TM.
claim: Surface EMG amplitude has important limitations as a proxy for force sharing and hypertrophy.
limitations: Not a conversion formula from activation to set credit.

title: Low-load bench press and push-up induce similar muscle hypertrophy and strength gain
authors: Kikuchi N, Nakazato K.
claim: Bench press and appropriately loaded push-ups increased pectoral and triceps thickness over eight weeks.
limitations: Small sample of young men; no exact synergist set equivalence.

title: Effects of Horizontal and Incline Bench Press on Neuromuscular Adaptations in Untrained Young Men
authors: Chaves SFN, Rocha-JÚnior VA, EncarnaÇÃo IGA, Martins-Costa HC, Freitas EDS, Coelho DB, Franco FSC, Loenneke JP, Bottaro M, Ferreira-JÚnior JB.
claim: Incline and horizontal bench pressing produced some regional differences in pectoral growth.
limitations: Supports distinguishing bench angles, not separate regional muscle IDs or exact fractions.

title: Effects of squat training with different depths on lower limb muscle volumes
authors: Kubo K, Ikebukuro T, Yata H.
claim: Squat depth affected gluteal/adductor growth; knee extensors grew but hamstrings did not significantly grow.
limitations: Study of barbell squats; leg press, hack squat and lunge application is an inference.

title: Hip thrust and back squat training elicit similar gluteus muscle hypertrophy and transfer similarly to the deadlift
authors: Plotkin DL, Rodas MA, Vigotsky AD, McIntosh MC, Breeze E, Ubrik R, Robitzsch C, Agyin-Birikorang A, Mattingly ML, Michel JM, Kontos NJ, Lennon S, Frugé AD, Wilburn CM, Weimar WH, Bashir A, Beyers RJ, Henselmans M, Contreras BM, Roberts MD.
claim: Squats and hip thrusts increased gluteal size; thigh growth favored squats; hamstrings and glute med/min changed little.
limitations: Untrained participants; not all machine designs or techniques.

title: Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position
authors: Maeo S, Wu Y, Huang M, Sakurai H, Kusagawa Y, Sugiyama T, Kanehisa H, Isaka T.
claim: Overhead cable elbow extension produced greater triceps growth than neutral-arm extension.
limitations: Both train triceps; no numerical set multiplier is established.

title: Dumbbell versus cable lateral raises for lateral deltoid hypertrophy: an experimental study
authors: Larsen S, Wolf M, Schoenfeld BJ, Sandberg NØ, Fredriksen AB, Kristiansen BS, van den Tillaar R, Swinton PA, Falch HN.
claim: Dumbbell and cable lateral raises increased lateral deltoid thickness with similar observed changes.
limitations: Matched ROM; does not establish identical results for every cable height or machine.

title: Single vs. Multi-Joint Resistance Exercises: Effects on Muscle Strength and Hypertrophy
authors: Gentil P, Soares S, Bottaro M.
claim: Lat pulldowns and curls both increased elbow-flexor thickness in untrained men.
limitations: Conflicting comparative literature and muscle measurement limitations prevent exact fractions.

title: Variation of muscle moment arms with elbow and forearm position
authors: Murray WM, Delp SL, Buchanan TS.
claim: Elbow and forearm positions alter elbow-flexor moment arms, including the biceps supination advantage.
limitations: Cadaver/model biomechanics; not hypertrophy or 0.25/0.5/1 calibration.

title: Specificity of resistance training responses in neck muscle size and strength
authors: Conley MS, Stone MH, Nimmons M, Dudley GA.
claim: Specific head-extension training induced cervical hypertrophy beyond conventional resistance training.
limitations: Evidence for extension does not establish flexion/lateral-flexion effects or set equivalence.

title: Weightlifting pulling derivatives: rationale for implementation and application
authors: Suchomel TJ, Comfort P, Stone MH.
claim: Weightlifting pulls and their derivatives use coordinated hip, knee and ankle extension; catches distinguish full lifts.
limitations: Power/technique review; hypertrophy-equivalent set accounting is especially uncertain.

title: A review of the specificity of exercises designed for conditioning the lumbar extensors
authors: Steele J, Bruce-Low S, Smith D.
claim: Lumbar extensor adaptations depend on whether exercise loads spinal extension specifically or permits hip motion.
limitations: Review emphasizes specificity; exact hypertrophy set equivalents remain unknown.

title: Development of lumbar extension strength: Effect of pelvic stabilization during resistance training
authors: Mayer JM, Graves JE, Udermann BE, Ploutz-Snyder LL.
claim: Lumbar extension strength increased with and without pelvic stabilization when training/testing used the same device.
limitations: Strength is not hypertrophy; counters a universal claim that restraint is always necessary.

title: The impact of resistance training on gluteus maximus hypertrophy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Krause Neto W, Krause TLV, Gama EF.
claim: Resistance training including hip thrusts, squats and some other hip extension exercises increases glute max size.
limitations: Heterogeneous protocols do not establish an allocation table for each variation.

title: Perceived loading and muscle activity during hip strengthening exercises: comparison of elastic resistance and machine exercises
authors: Brandt M, Jakobsen MD, Thorborg K, Sundstrup E, Jay K, Andersen LL.
claim: Hip abduction/adduction with bands and machines can be performed with comparable perceived loading; EMG was measured.
limitations: Used for exercise identification and feasibility only, not precise credits or growth.

title: Core Muscle Activity During Physical Fitness Exercises: A Systematic Review
authors: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM.
claim: Core exercise studies measure activity in rectus abdominis, obliques and spinal muscles.
limitations: EMG-only synthesis; cannot rank hypertrophy or assign exact set fractions.

title: Triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training
authors: Kinoshita M, Maeo S, Kobayashi Y, Eihara Y, Ono M, Sato M, Sugiyama T, Kanehisa H, Isaka T.
claim: Standing calf raises grew gastrocnemius more than seated raises; soleus grew similarly in both positions.
limitations: Does not establish that standing soleus sets should count half; this remains source calibration.

title: Wrist Resistance Training Improves Motor Control and Strength
authors: Chu E, Kim YS, Hill G, Kim YH, Kim CK, Shim JK.
claim: Direction-specific wrist resistance training improved wrist strength and motor control.
limitations: Strength outcomes do not establish hypertrophy equivalence or exact wrist exercise credits.

title: Greater Hamstrings Muscle Hypertrophy but Similar Damage Protection after Training at Long versus Short Muscle Lengths
authors: Maeo S, Huang M, Wu Y, Sakurai H, Kusagawa Y, Sugiyama T, Kanehisa H, Isaka T.
claim: Seated and prone leg curls increased hamstring size, with greater biarticular growth in the seated condition.
limitations: Does not establish exact per-set credit or equivalence across all leg curl devices.

title: Comparison Between Shoulder Flexed and Extended Positions in Elbow Flexion Resistance Training on Regional Hypertrophy and Maximum Strength: Preacher versus Bayesian Cable Curls
authors: Attarieh P, Nunes JP, Khani S, Negahdar S, Goli A, Nazarirad H, Nazarirad S, Mojtahedi S, Nosaka K, Soori R.
claim: Preacher and Bayesian cable curls with matched resistance profiles increased biceps and brachialis thickness without a significant between-condition difference.
limitations: Small ten-week trial in young men; does not establish a precise 1-to-0.5 allocation or universal superiority of either shoulder position.

title: Anatomy and Physiology: Muscles Of The Pectoral Girdle And Upper Limbs
authors: OpenStax, Rice University
claim: Upper-limb and scapular muscles have different joint actions; wrist actions differ from elbow flexion.
limitations: Anatomical actions support classification; all numerical set credits are editorial inference, not measured by this textbook.

title: Anatomy and Physiology: Appendicular Muscles Of The Pelvic Girdle And Lower Limbs
authors: OpenStax, Rice University
claim: Hip, knee and ankle muscles differ in their primary joint actions and biarticular geometry.
limitations: Anatomical actions support classification; all numerical set credits are editorial inference, not measured by this textbook.

title: Anatomy and Physiology: Axial Muscles Of The Abdominal Wall And Thorax
authors: OpenStax, Rice University
claim: Rectus abdominis flexes the trunk; obliques participate in rotation and lateral flexion.
limitations: Anatomical actions support classification; all numerical set credits are editorial inference, not measured by this textbook.

title: Anatomy and Physiology: Axial Muscles Of The Head Neck And Back
authors: OpenStax, Rice University
claim: Neck flexion, extension and lateral flexion involve distinct muscles; spinal extensors extend the vertebral column.
limitations: Anatomical actions support classification; all numerical set credits are editorial inference, not measured by this textbook.

title: PANDR-5™ Model — Guide Sheet
authors: PANDR-5 model owner
claim: Guide Sheet J5:K23 encodes the preserved 26-exercise calibration catalog and 1/0.5/0.25 credits.
limitations: Owner model, not independent scientific validation; live formulas verified with Google Sheets connector on 2026-09-18.
